spans.text: Abishai were once the fiendish servants of the Queen of Evil Dragons, worshiping her since her reign in the Old World. When she split herself into five aspects, fled, and was consequently lost to the Hells, the abishai risked being driven out by a lack of purpose. Instead, they were rallied under the five Grand Abishai - the direct servants of the queen. These leaders promised to one day free the stolen divine power of their goddess and return the queen to her complete form, and in doing so they held together the abishai forces.

When the aspects began developing individuality, the Grands each took on their own interpretation of the events at hand: while one might long for the return of their queen, another might have felt that the newly formed “children of the dragon queen” - the five new entities who had come forth from her aspects - served as her new legacy. The abishai alliances became complicated, with each grand abishai seeking its corresponding aspect for their own purposes. Those who found them offered themselves and their followers to that aspect, hoping they might one day rise to the same glorious heights that the queen had.

The abishai of the Old World were fiends born from the souls who endeared themselves to the dragon queen in life. These included her cultists, followers, and those who sacrificed themselves to her as food upon her many attempts to return to the Material Plane. Those who died in her favor became abishai in the Hells. Now, their ranks are maintained in a similar way, but through fiendish contracts with the Grand Abishai and their followers, who seek souls to transform and fill their ranks in the afterlife.

The five aspects of the queen were once of one mind, separated only in form. They shared her divine power and would intend to reconnect once they passed through the Divine Curtain. To their chagrin, they were intercepted in the Material Plane by Opiuchus and their divine power was carved from them - with it, their ability to reform was lost. They scattered, and took humanoid form to avoid being caught in their vulnerable state.

They would eventually be separated for so long that their old identity faded from their mind and individuality overtook them, along with new ideals, ambitions and powers. In the modern world they regained their divine power and draconic forms thanks to the efforts of a certain adventuring guild, but their individual motivations remain, and they do not wish to throw themselves back into their old form - now thought of among them as their “mother.”
